To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
δ-α-tocompherol supplementation did not attenuate the oxidative stress in iron-overloaded rats.
high δ-α-tocoherol supplementation in iron-overloaded rats resulted in increased vitamin C and genotoxicity, and did not ameliorate oxidative damage.
δ-α-toco-pherol supplementation at high doses (10× RDI) to iron-overloaded rats did not reduce the oxidative stress in the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible adverse effect of high doses of δ-tocopherol on the liver of iron-overloaded animals.
the possible adverse effects of high δ-α-tocoherol intake on the liver of iron overload animals.
the adverse effects of δ-α-Tocopherol in iron overload.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

high doses of vitamin E (α-tocopherols) supplementation in iron overload did not ameliorate the hepatic iron overload and oxidative damage, but rather enhanced oxidative liver damage, as evidenced by increased production of the genotoxin 8-OH-dG.

high dose δ-α-tocompherol supplementation in iron-overload rats may have a possible adverse effect on the hepatic iron overload by enhancing the production of vitamin C, which in turn may enhance the production of the genotoxin 8-OHdg.
high dose δ-α-tocompherol supplementation in iron-overloaded rats may not be beneficial in terms of ameliorating oxidative stress and liver function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high doses of δ-alpha-tocopheryl succinate (α-tocopheryl) may be harmful to rats with hepatic iron overload.
the use of high doses of δ-tocopherol as a remedy for oxidative stress in the iron overload condition should be avoided.
high doses of δ-tocopherol may not be beneficial in iron-overloaded patients, and may even be detrimental.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high dose of δ-α- tocopherol supplementation in rats with iron overload does not ameliorate oxidative stress and that high doses of vitamin C may have a genotoxic effect.
high δ-α-tocoherol intake in iron overload may have a negative effect on oxidative liver damage.
high doses of α-tocopherols should be avoided in the management of oxidative liver damage.
